schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE EMP (NAME INT, DEPT INT, EMP INT);
CREATE TABLE DEPT (DEPT INT, LOC INT, MGR INT);
q1: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X WHERE (X.EMP, X.DEPT) IN (SELECT Y.MGR, Y.DEPT FROM DEPT AS Y WHERE Y.LOC = 3)
q2: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X WHERE (X.EMP, X.DEPT) IN (SELECT Y.MGR, Y.DEPT FROM DEPT AS Y WHERE Y.LOC = 3)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X
counterexample: INSERT INTO DEPT (DEPT, LOC, MGR) VALUES (1, 2, 101); INSERT INTO EMP (NAME, DEPT, EMP) VALUES (1, 1, 102);
explanation: Q1 filters employees based on the manager of a department located at a specific location (LOC = 3), while Q2 selects all employees without any filtering.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there are employees in departments that do not have a manager located at LOC = 3.
